messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — gpu-pool eu-west-1 reporting sustained queue depth and token latency spikes. 90p token latency > 3s, error rate up 4%. Paged on-call: @alice nguyen.

alice nguyen: I’m oncall and joining the bridge now. pulling metrics.

miguel santos: I’m nearby — looks like autoscaler didn’t spin extra nodes after the config drift at 03:10 UTC. checking controller logs.

tara patel: Oncall SRE here — created bridge https://call.redwood/bridge/1785554321. Can we temporarily divert non-prod + low-priority traffic?

ops-james: Heads up to CS: which customers are affected? we should notify any customers near SLA. @ellen rao can you pull recent error reports?

ellen rao: Two customers (acme-ai, travellytics) filed 500s around 03:12 and 03:14 UTC. Both use dedicated inference on eu-west-1. I’ll open support tickets and flag for urgent outreach.

product-sam: Are we seeing model fallbacks? any graceful degradation? customers asking about mem/cold-starts.

alice nguyen: Fallbacks were triggered for a subset of requests — some routed to a smaller q8 quantized variant which increased latency. Root cause: autoscaler not honoring maxSurge after the rollout earlier.

miguel santos: Quick mitigation plan: 1) drain batch/predict jobs on eu-west pool 2) bump autoscaler min nodes + override maxSurge 3) failover some routes to eu-central until capacity stabilizes. Executing step 1 now.

incident-bot: ACTION: drain job queues from pool eu-west-gpu-batch (cmd run by miguel santos).

miguel santos: Ran: ```kubectl patch clusterautoscaler eu-west --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/scaleDown","value":{"enabled":false}}]'``` — autoscaler patch applied. bumping desiredNodes +10.

alice nguyen: I flipped routing policy to prefer eu-central for non-dedicated tier. Observed queue length drop ~12% in last 2m.

tara patel: Monitoring: 90p latency falling but still above SLO (target 2s). keeping bridge open. Noticing preemption spikes on spot instances — moving some pods to on-demand pool.

ops-james: CS notified acme-ai and travellytics with interim status note. Both asked for ETA — we advised 1 hour to stabilize.

ellen rao: Support tickets created: SUP-4312 (acme-ai), SUP-4313 (travellytics). I added error traces and correlating request IDs.

product-sam: Requesting post-incident review and clear customer communication template. Assigning owner for comms?

alice nguyen: Postmortem owner: @miguel santos. I’ll add initial timeline and action items. Proposed postmortem slot: tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Jira INF-2345 created for tracking.

miguel santos: I’ll own the writeup. Immediate action items: - AUT-1: fix autoscaler rollout test (owner: miguel, due 2025-07-03) - INF-2: add routing escape hatch to prefer geo-fallback (owner: alice, due 2025-07-02) - SPT-1: customer follow-up templates (owner: ellen, due 2025-07-01). I’ll link these to INF-2345.

alice nguyen: Also adding a reliability card to the roadmap for multi-region quick-failover runbook.

tara patel: Marking incident severity P1 -> downgraded to P2 at 03:45 UTC since error rate dropped and customers reachable.

ops-james: thumbs up. Please post the action item list to the incident doc and ping me when the postmortem is scheduled.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity P2, mitigation in progress, postmortem scheduled (INF-2345).

product-sam: Thanks team. After postmortem we should produce a short customer-facing RCA for affected accounts.

alice nguyen: Agreed. Closing bridge once autoscaler stabilization confirmed. Will update thread when closed. :thumbsup:

miguel santos: follow-ups: verify autoscaler e2e test, add stronger canary checks for rollout, and schedule a DR test for region failover (owner: miguel, target: Q3). I’ll drop links to PRs and logs in INF-2345. :eyes:
